headline: EU AI Act: your chatbot has to say it is AI - grace period ends 2 December
summary: Companies with AI products interacting with EU users face fines up to 3% of global turnover if they don't disclose AI use by December 2, 2026. This applies even without an EU office.
details: Article 50 of the EU AI Act, which mandates disclosure for AI systems, has been in effect since August 2, 2026, for products interacting with EU users. The grace period for systems already on the market before this date concludes on December 2, 2026.

Non-compliance with this marking duty can result in significant penalties, with fines potentially reaching up to 3% of a company's global turnover. This regulation applies broadly to SaaS founders shipping chat features, AI content tools, onboarding bots, and support agents.

Crucially, the Act's jurisdiction follows the users, meaning companies do not need an EU office to be subject to its requirements. Any product or service used by an EU citizen falls under the scope of Article 50.

Resources like obligation maps and disclosure wording templates are available to help companies navigate these requirements. A free obligation checker can also assist in assessing a company's current compliance standing.

headline: Instagram taken down during protests: Guide to backup content & stay connected
summary: Instagram outages are impacting communication during protests, potentially erasing crucial evidence. A new guide provides practical steps for immediate content backup and setting up decentralized communication channels.
details: Instagram has been taken down in several cities during recent protests, often within 24 hours of demonstrations starting. These unexpected outages leave activists without vital communication channels and risk the loss of important evidence, such as photos and videos.

To counter this, a practical guide offers solutions, including a simple script to immediately back up your 30 most recent Instagram posts (images or videos). Running this script before any perceived interruption can help preserve your content.

The guide also details how to create a personal Mastodon node on a Linux system. This step-by-step process allows users to set up their own micro-blogging platform, providing an independent communication channel.

Once configured, accessing your node via its IP address enables account creation, giving you a personal micro-blog. This decentralized approach ensures your communications cannot be easily shut down by internet providers or social media platforms.
